questions.q: What happens to detail records when their master record is deleted in a master-detail relationship?
options: They are also deleted -- Salesforce's documentation describes this as cascade delete
Nothing; detail records are always preserved
They are automatically reparented to a different master
They become lookup records instead
questions.explain: Per Salesforce's object reference, deleting a master record also deletes its related detail records -- this is cascade delete, and it has no equivalent on lookup relationships.

questions.q: Why can't a master-detail detail record have its own sharing rules, manual sharing, or queues?
options: Because detail records are read-only by default
Because only standard objects support sharing rules
Because master-detail relationships disable all automation on the detail object
Because those mechanisms require an independent Owner field, and a detail record's Owner field isn't available -- it's automatically set to the master record's owner
questions.explain: The lesson explains that sharing rules, manual sharing, and queues all depend on an independent Owner field, which detail records don't have -- they inherit the master's owner and sharing instead.

questions.q: What is the single most common reason architects choose master-detail over lookup, according to this lesson?
options: Master-detail relationships are faster to query
Lookup relationships cannot be created between custom objects
The need for a native roll-up summary field, which has no equivalent on lookup relationships
Master-detail relationships are required for all custom objects
questions.explain: The lesson identifies the roll-up summary field -- which only works on master-detail relationships -- as the single most common deciding factor toward choosing master-detail.

questions.q: By default, can a detail record's master be changed after it's set in a master-detail relationship?
options: No, reparenting is restricted by default, though admins can enable an 'Allow reparenting' option for custom-object master-detail relationships
Yes, always, with no configuration needed
Only on standard objects
Only if no roll-up summary field exists anywhere in the org
questions.explain: The lesson states that reparenting is restricted by default, but administrators can explicitly turn on an 'Allow reparenting' override for custom-object master-detail relationships.

questions.q: A Case needs its own queue-based assignment independent of its related Account. Per the decision framework in this lesson, what does that requirement signal?
options: Master-detail is required, since every Case belongs to an Account
This requirement is incompatible with master-detail, since detail records can't have independent ownership or queues -- lookup (or a different model) is needed
Roll-up summary fields will resolve this automatically
This requirement has no bearing on relationship type
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly uses this exact example: needing independent queue-based assignment is incompatible with master-detail's forced ownership inheritance, so lookup is the appropriate choice.
